newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Blue chip gains propel Manila shares up at close.
newsitem.headline: Blue chip gains propel Manila shares up at close.

text.p: Philippine shares closed higher on Thursday despite a soft opening buoyed by blue chip buying ahead of the release of first quarter GNP figures later in the day, traders said.
The main index settled 35.94 points higher, or 1.32 percent, at 2,758.61 points.

"There was a lot of good news namely the cut in overnight borrowing and lending rates, reduction in full-year inflation targets, and a possibly good first quarter GNP figure that did market sentiment good," said Jose Ricardo Garcia, executive vice-president at Diversified Securities.
"There was a repositioning in blue chips, the old reliables, before the release of GNP which could already be factored in," said Helen Alvarez, research director at All Asia Securities.
Despite its six-day runup, thin volume, on Thursday just 1.79 billion pesos, continued to characterised the market.
Top five gainers were blue chip issues Meralco B, Philippine National Bank, Ayala Land Inc, PLDT and Petron Corp PCOR PS.
But in the broad market, decliners still outnumbered gainers 62 to 50 with 73 issues unchanged.
Regina Capital Development vice-president Allan Araullo said the market's performance on Friday will hinge on the GNP results.
"We can still move upward especially if the GNP figure is way beyond expectations," Araullo said.
